thread:
Alex M.: hey, getting a spike of 401s from a customer hitting /v1/submit, looks like signature verification failed intermittently. pasted few lines from the flagging service:
```
ERROR verify_jwt: signature verification failed, kid not found in cached JWKS (kid=key_2026_04)
TRACE request_id=ry-01a user_id=acct_123 path=/v1/submit
```
Also see valid requests around the same time that succeed.

Samir K.: thanks. do we know if that customer uses key rotation? could be a race between rotation and our jwks cache. what is our JWKS cache TTL on the gateway?

Alex M.: they do rotate daily. gateway config shows jwks_cache_ttl=86400 (24h) for production route. :grimacing: but the rotation happens via our key service every ~6h for that customer.

Liz Chen: ah -- we set 24h by default after last perf run to reduce jwks fetches. but that is too long for customers rotating frequently. sounds like when they rotated the kid changed, our cached JWKS doesn't contain new kid -> verification fails.

security-bot: automated note: JWKS refresh attempted but skipped due to cache TTL. next scheduled refresh in 23h 59m.

Samir K.: can we repro quickly? alex, can you share the raw jwt header & signature when it fails? specifically the kid value.

Alex M.: pasted anonymized header from one failing request:
```
{"alg":"RS256","typ":"JWT","kid":"key_2026_04"}
```
and our cached jwks.json (excerpt) only has key_2026_02 and key_2026_03.

Liz Chen: repro plan: 1) simulate rotation: publish new key to key-service with kid=X 2) keep gateway jwks cache warm but with TTL=24h 3) send signed JWT with new kid -> expect kid-not-found -> 401.

Samir K.: also noticed verifier library requires exp/leeway config. are we rejecting due to small leeway combined with token issuance clock? maybe some hosts had skew. what does the verifier config look like?

Alex M.: verifier: leeway_seconds=0 in prod for strictness. customer rotates keys from an automation that issues tokens a couple seconds earlier than our validator host (clock skew up to ~45s observed in monitoring). so even if kid present, exp/nbf checks might fail. when both occur together it's messy.

Liz Chen: ok two separate failure modes colliding: (A) stale JWKS cache -> kid not found -> signature error, (B) zero leeway -> exp/nbf rejects for small clock skew. we'll need fixes for both.

ops-oncall: short-term mitigation I pushed: 1) lowered jwks_cache_ttl from 24h -> 5m for the affected gateway route, 2) added fallback to do a real-time jwks fetch when kid not found (sync fetch, logs it), 3) set leeway_seconds=60 temporarily for verifier. rolled at 1758003400.

Alex M.: testing now — after the hotfix the failing requests are being accepted. logs show real-time fetch returned the new key and verification passed. :thumbsup:

Samir K.: good. long-term action items: - make jwks_cache_ttl tunable per-customer rotation frequency, - add metrics/alert when verifier does a "remote JWKS fetch due to unknown kid", - add a safe default leeway (30s) and document reasoning, - consider background refresh on rotation event from key-service.

Liz Chen: will open a follow-up RFC for jwks caching policy + rotation webhook. will also add a note in the customer onboarding docs about recommended rotation cadence vs cache TTL.

security-bot: Incident ticket created: SEC-2026-338 (priority P2) with links to logs and the hotfix revert plan.

Alex M.: thanks everyone. filing a small postmortem later with timeline and exact repro steps.

ops-oncall: leaving the temporary leeway in place for 24h while we monitor. will revert once metrics stable. if anyone sees a rise in replay/latency, ping me.
